question: Can a Christian become wholly holy in this life?

answers.label: Yes: entire sanctification, perfect love, can be given in this life
No: only Christ was without sin; we are made perfect after death

overview.text: Clement of Alexandria doubted that anyone but Christ is perfect in everything while still human. Augustine, against Pelagius, said the same: sinlessness is possible by grace, but no one but Christ has had it.
Reformed and Catholic teaching both place full holiness after this life: at death, or through purification after death.
Wesley taught that "perfect love", entire sanctification, can be received in this life by faith. The Holiness churches made it an article of faith.

quotes.author: Clement of Alexandria
quotes.english: One is made perfect as devout, as patient, as self-controlled, as a worker, as a martyr, as one who knows God. But perfect in all of them together, I do not know if any human being is, while still human, except only the one who put on humanity for our sake.
quotes.original: τελειοῦται γοῦν τις καὶ ὡς εὐλαβὴς καὶ ὡς ὑπομονητικὸς καὶ ὡς ἐγκρατὴς καὶ ὡς ἐργάτης καὶ ὡς μάρτυς καὶ ὡς γνωστικός· πάντα δὲ ὁμοῦ τέλειος οὐκ οἶδ’ εἴ τις ἀνθρώπων, ἔτι ἄνθρωπος ὤν, πλὴν μόνον ὁ δἰ ἡμᾶς ἄνθρωπον ἐνδυσάμενος.
quotes.context: Clement also describes the mature Christian, his "true gnostic", as free from passion and perfect (Stromata 7).

quotes.author: Pelagius (quoted by Augustine)
quotes.work: Letter, quoted in Augustine, On the Proceedings of Pelagius
quotes.english: By the judgment of fourteen bishops our definition was approved, in which we said that a person can be without sin and easily keep God's commandments, if he wishes.
quotes.original: quattuordecim episcoporum sententia definitio nostra comprobata est, qua diximus posse hominem sine peccato esse et dei mandata facile custodire, si uelit.
quotes.context: For Pelagius, sinlessness is possible by our own will, with the help God gives in nature and teaching.

quotes.author: Augustine of Hippo
quotes.work: On the Merits and Forgiveness of Sins
quotes.english: Those who say that a person can be without sin in this life should not be opposed at once with careless rashness. For if we deny that it can be, we will take away from both the free choice of man, who wills it, and the power or mercy of God, who brings it about by his help. But it is one question whether it can be, another whether it is.
quotes.original: Nam qui dicunt esse posse in hac uita hominem sine peccato, non est eis continuo incauta temeritate obsistendum. si enim esse posse negauerimus, et hominis libero arbitrio, qui hoc uolendo appetit, et dei uirtuti uel misericordiae, qui hoc adiuuando efficit, derogabimus. sed alia quaestio est, utrum esse possit, alia utrum sit
quotes.context: Augustine grants it is possible by grace, but denies that anyone but Christ has done it.

quotes.author: Augustine of Hippo
quotes.work: On the Perfection of Human Righteousness
quotes.english: But it is one thing to be without sin, which in this life is said of the Only-begotten alone; another to be without blame, which could be said of many righteous people even in this life.
quotes.original: sed aliud est esse sine peccato, quod de solo in hac uita unigenito dictum est, aliud esse sine querella, quod de multis iustis etiam in hac uita dici potuit
quotes.context: Augustine answers Caelestius, Pelagius's disciple. 1 John 1:8 was his constant text: "If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves."

quotes.author: Council of Carthage
quotes.english: It was also resolved: as Saint John the apostle says, 'If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us' (1 John 1:8); whoever thinks this should be taken to mean that we ought to say we have sin out of humility, and not because it is truly so, let him be anathema. ... It was also resolved: whoever says that in the Lord's Prayer the saints say 'Forgive us our debts' (Matthew 6:12) not for themselves, because this petition is no longer necessary for them, but for the other sinners among their people, let him be anathema.
quotes.original: Item placuit, quod ait S. Ioannes Apostolus: Si dixerimus, quia peccatum non habemus, nos ipsos seducimus, et veritas in nobis non est: quisquis sic accipiendum putaverit, ut dicat propter humilitatem oportere dici, nos habere peccatum, non quia vere ita est, A. S. ... Item placuit, ut quicunque dixerit, in oratione dominica ideo dicere sanctos: Dimitte nobis debita nostra, ut non pro seipsis hoc dicant, quia non est eis iam necessaria ista petitio, sed pro aliis qui sunt in suo populo peccatores, A. S.
quotes.context: Carthage (418), canons 6 and 7 of the anti-Pelagian decrees: even the saints pray 'forgive us' for themselves, because even the saints still sin.

source.edition: Denzinger, Enchiridion symbolorum, 11th ed. (1911), nos. 106 and 107

quotes.author: Westminster Assembly
quotes.english: This sanctification is throughout, in the whole man; yet imperfect in this life, there abiding still some remnants of corruption in every part
quotes.original: This sanctification is throughout, in the whole man; yet imperfect in this life, there abiding still some remnants of corruption in every part
quotes.context: The Reformed view: holiness grows, but sin remains until death.

quotes.author: Catechism of the Catholic Church
quotes.english: All who die in God's grace and friendship, but still imperfectly purified, are indeed assured of their eternal salvation; but after death they undergo purification, so as to achieve the holiness necessary to enter the joy of heaven.
quotes.original: All who die in God's grace and friendship, but still imperfectly purified, are indeed assured of their eternal salvation; but after death they undergo purification, so as to achieve the holiness necessary to enter the joy of heaven.
quotes.context: The Catholic view: those not yet fully purified at death are made holy after death (purgatory).

quotes.author: John Wesley
quotes.english: It is thus that we wait for entire sanctification, for a full salvation from all our sins, from pride, self-will, anger, unbelief; or, as the apostle expresses it, go on to perfection. But what is perfection? The word has various senses: here it means, perfect love. It is love excluding sin: love filling the heart, taking up the whole capacity of the soul.
quotes.original: It is thus that we wait for entire sanctification, for a full salvation from all our sins, from pride, self-will, anger, unbelief; or, as the apostle expresses it, go on to perfection. But what is perfection? The word has various senses: here it means, perfect love. It is love excluding sin: love filling the heart, taking up the whole capacity of the soul.
quotes.context: Wesley taught that perfect love can be given in this life, by faith. He did not mean freedom from all mistakes or weakness.

quotes.author: Church of the Nazarene
quotes.english: We believe that entire sanctification is that act of God, subsequent to regeneration, by which believers are made free from original sin, or depravity
quotes.original: We believe that entire sanctification is that act of God, subsequent to regeneration, by which believers are made free from original sin, or depravity
quotes.context: The Holiness churches that grew from Methodism.

source.edition: Church of the Nazarene, Articles of Faith (Manual 2023)
